As scientists track how El Niño will impact winter weather this year, what if this massive Pacific warm wave never turned off? Normally, El Niño shifts global jet streams by dumping ocean heat into the atmosphere. But if it became permanent, global weather patterns would lock in place. Severe, endless rainstorms would batter southern coastal regions, while vital agricultural heartlands faced perpetual drought. Cold deep-sea currents would stop rising, threatening marine ecosystems worldwide. Could humanity adapt to a world with permanent climate shifts? Follow for more what-ifs.

Based on today's news: What Could El Niño Mean for New Jersey’s Winter? - Rutgers Climate and Energy Institute (RCEI)
